title: We Will Meet Again
subtitle: Until we meet again, in another time, in another place.

items.text: The party journeys along the river for a long time, but the night never falls.
Most of them are in a hurry to leave—the same desire as before, but now much stronger than ever before, more than enough to bring the long-awaited harmony of a common purpose to the team.
And no one dares mention their experiences for the rest of the trip.

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Let's make camp after we get out of the forest. What do you say?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I'm fine with it. How are you feeling, Mr. Jurien?

items.speaker: Jurien
items.text: I'm fine with that.
A few still harbor a lingering curiosity, one they endure for a long time, and until unable to resist, they turn around to see if the ancient city on the mountainside is still in sight.
But while this is not a story where those who look back might turn into pillars of salt, there remains no trace of the strange city that should have still been in view.
And as they walk onward, the revived river known as the Pèilín too has changed its appearance.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Madam, the river ...
The once-wide river invisibly splits into slender tributaries behind them, spread out across the lush spring meadows like a rope net.
Even if they wanted to find it, they might never distinguish the one that would lead them back.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: What is it?

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: The compass is working!

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: Great!
Their fellow traveler excitedly raises his hands, briefly blocking Yenisei's gaze from Bessmert.
The girl takes advantage of the situation and withdraws the words she cannot say. She only gently shakes her head.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Nothing. Let's move.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: The compass is working, which means we can rely on the map again.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Oh, that's good. As for the book I'm going to write ...

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Yes? Have you decided the title?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Yes. I will call it ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: "Notes on Shuòrì."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Notes on Shuòrì ...

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Yes, that's the title.
She flips over a page and continues reading.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "The title is actually not a good choice for a book on geographical discoveries."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "On one hand, there is no doubt that 'Shuòrì' is a difficult word for the target readers of this book."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "On the other hand, the word 'Notes,' in most cases, is used to describe the collections of informal essays. They usually record the daily talks of professional writers, and thus include a variety of ideas and inspirations."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "As a geographer, however, I don't possess enough knowledge of literature to write the real 'Notes,' nor does the assistant who takes dictations from me, unfortunately ..."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Haha ...

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "Even so, we have decided to use these words for the title. Postscript: The title has also been included in the first draft we sent to the editors of Motherland Documentary and the Department of Publication Review."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: The next page is missing. Let me see ...

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Oh, found it.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "June 4, sunny. I never knew the journey back to Omsk would take so long. My assistant and I set off from Yekaterinburg last year, and we didn't arrive until now ..."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "In Omsk, we met the governor again. I left him some drafts of this book in return for the help from the local Scientific Research Association."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "Those drafts have recorded the steppe ecosystem around the Om River in detail. For example, before we arrived in Omsk, we followed a herd of sheep across the river. The wool on their tails was apparently matted."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "I recorded this detail because the way they crossed the water was almost a miracle. It is known to all that sheep can be easily drowned because their thick wool holds them back in water."

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: "Yet things seemed different for those sheep. They had been trained by the local herders and were able to cross the river swiftly, as if they were only several balls of cotton floating on the water ..."

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: "... When they came to the shore, I noticed that their hooves were in the shape of a round cake with one slice missing."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hmm ...

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: "They climbed out of the water with their little cake hooves, shook themselves dry, and continued on to the next pasture, never hesitant to go forward, never looking back."

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: "Seeing all these, I hope I will be as determined as these sheep in my future journey ..."

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: "Today's article was an extract from a geographic manuscript from St. Pavlov Foundation Far East Branch, recorded by Yenisei."

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: "Next is the news broadcast ..."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mmm ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Radio?

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Yes, I'm here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I ... What time is it now?

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: It's 4:15 p.m.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The nap went on a little longer than I thought.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Yes. How are you feeling?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Think I had a dream. Many animals were jumping over a broken bridge.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: I read you a story which has zebras and sheep in it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Zebras and sheep?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't remember that ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hmm?
Excuse me. Is Timekeeper in the room?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I am.
May I come in? There is something I need to confirm with you ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm sorry, who's that?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hmm? It's me, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I might have taken too long a nap. Never mind, please come in.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, you don't look very well. Are you alright?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's ok. I had a weird dream.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's going on?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Oh, it's a letter from the Foundation. A colleague from the Russian branch was transferred to the headquarters today. She has shown a strong willingness to perform long-term field missions ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Thus, the headquarters intends to transfer her to the Timekeeper Squad. Would you have a meeting with her? It is said that she is experienced in geographical exploration and survival in the wilderness. She could be a great helper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Geographical exploration? What's her name?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Please hold on. Let me check her file here.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And her name is ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yenisei.
